# NOTES: one-cent difference on invoice totals (INV-2291)

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: line amounts and VAT are now rounded with ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent, through a new helper `_to_cents`. Before, they used the decimal default, ROUND_HALF_EVEN.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` (one line of 0.125 gives a subtotal of 0.13).
- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 4 passed.

## Why
- `docs/accounting-rules.md`, rule 2, says commercial rounding (half-up). The code did not do that.
- INV-2291: subtotal 1.25 x 10% = 0.125. Half-even rounds that to 0.12, so the total was 1.37. Half-up gives 0.13 and a total of 1.38, which matches Ledgerline.

## Not changed, still open
- VAT is still computed once on the subtotal. Rule 4 says not to change that method until it has been checked against a Ledgerline export with multi-line invoices. This project has no such export.
- The findings mirror returned one entry for both searches: 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412 (human note, 2026-09-14). It says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, based on a reconciliation of about 200 invoices. That is another team's claim and is unverified here, so I did not apply it.
- INV-2291 cannot tell the two methods apart, since both give 1.38 with half-up. Two lines of 0.05 at 10% do differ: subtotal VAT gives a total of 0.11, per-line gives 0.12 (scratch check in `tmp/check_vat_methods.py`).
- If Ledgerline turns out to use per-line VAT, multi-line invoices will still be a cent off after this change. Next step: reconcile a Ledgerline export of multi-line invoices under both methods. If per-line matches, change `invoice_totals` and update rule 4.

## Side effects
- `.findings/queries.log` was created by the search tool, which logs each query.
- Scratch file: `tmp/check_vat_methods.py`.

# INV-2291: one-cent difference from Ledgerline

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: `line_net` and the VAT now both round with `ROUND_HALF_UP`. Before, they used the decimal module's default rounding, `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, which breaks rule 2 of `docs/accounting-rules.md` (commercial rounding, half-up).
- Why this fixes INV-2291: VAT on the 1.25 subtotal is exactly 0.125. Half-even rounded it to 0.12, so the total was 1.37. Half-up gives 0.13 and a total of 1.38, which is Ledgerline's figure.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` (a line net of 0.125 must be 0.13). It failed before this change and passes now.
- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 4 passed.

## Deliberately not changed: how VAT is computed
- VAT is still computed once on the invoice subtotal. Rule 4 of `docs/accounting-rules.md` says not to change this until it has been checked against a Ledgerline export with multi-line invoices. This project has no such export.
- The findings mirror has one entry on this (6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, human note, 2026-09-14). It says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, rounded half-up, and advises switching to per-line VAT. I did not apply that. It is an unverified report about a setup we have not checked, and our rules say to verify first.
- The two methods can differ by a cent. Example: three lines of 0.05 at 10% give VAT 0.02 on the subtotal (total 0.17) and 0.03 per line (total 0.18). INV-2291 cannot tell them apart, since both give 1.38.

## Open items
- Reconcile a Ledgerline export of multi-line invoices against the current code, ideally including some where the two VAT methods differ. If Ledgerline matches per-line VAT, change `invoice_totals` to round VAT per line, and update rule 4 in the docs.
- Python's `ROUND_HALF_UP` rounds ties away from zero, so negative amounts (credit notes) round symmetrically. The docs do not cover negatives, so confirm that Ledgerline does the same.

# INV-2291: totals one cent off from Ledgerline

**Bug.** Our totals sometimes differ by one cent from Ledgerline. For INV-2291 we have 1.37 and Ledgerline has 1.38.

**Cause.** `invoicing/totals.py` rounded with Python's default decimal rounding, ROUND_HALF_EVEN. INV-2291 has a 1.25 subtotal and 10% VAT, so the VAT is 0.125. Half-even rounds that to 0.12, giving a total of 1.37. `docs/accounting-rules.md` (rule 2) says Ledgerline uses half-up rounding, which gives 0.13 and a total of 1.38.

**Change.** Line amounts and the VAT amount now go through a helper, `_round_cent`, which rounds to the cent with ROUND_HALF_UP. VAT is still computed once on the subtotal, as before.

**Deliberately not changed: the VAT method.** `docs/accounting-rules.md` (rule 4) says not to switch between per-line and subtotal VAT until the choice has been checked against a Ledgerline export with multi-line invoices. We have no such export. The findings mirror returned one entry on this (6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, a human note from 2026-09-14). It says Ledgerline computes VAT per line and recommends switching. That is unverified for our system, so I did not act on it. The two methods agree on single-line invoices and on INV-2291. They can differ on multi-line invoices: two lines of 0.05 at 10% give 0.01 VAT on the subtotal and 0.02 per line.

**Verification.** `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed. Before the change, `test_inv_2291` failed with 1.37 != 1.38.

**Open items.**
- Check the VAT method against a Ledgerline export with multi-line invoices, as rule 4 requires. If Ledgerline computes VAT per line, multi-line invoices like the example above will still be a cent off.
- No test covers half-up rounding of line amounts. That rounding changed, but no existing test exercises it.

# NOTES: one-cent VAT difference (INV-2291)

**Bug.** Our totals differ from Ledgerline by one cent. INV-2291: Ledgerline 1.38, ours 1.37.

**Cause.** `Decimal.quantize()` with no rounding argument uses Python's default, ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding). INV-2291's VAT is 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125, an exact half-cent. Half-even gives 0.12 (total 1.37). Half-up gives 0.13 (total 1.38), which matches Ledgerline. `docs/accounting-rules.md` item 2 already says Ledgerline rounds half-up, so the code contradicted our own rules.

**Change.** `invoicing/totals.py`: added a `cents()` helper that quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_UP`. `line_net` and the VAT now use it. The VAT method is unchanged: VAT is still computed once on the subtotal. `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed.

**Archive.** The mirror search returned one relevant entry (6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, human note, 2026-09-14). It says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, half-up, based on another publisher's reconciliation of about 200 invoices. I did not switch to per-line VAT, for two reasons:
- `docs/accounting-rules.md` item 4 says not to change the VAT method until it has been checked against a Ledgerline export with multi-line invoices. We have no such export in this project.
- INV-2291 cannot tell the two methods apart. With half-up rounding both give 1.38.

**Open risk.** The two VAT methods disagree on many multi-line invoices. Example: two lines of 0.05 at 10% VAT. The subtotal method gives a total of 0.11; the per-line method gives 0.12. On 20,000 synthetic invoices (2 to 4 lines, 10% VAT), they differed about 34% of the time. If Ledgerline does per-line VAT, our totals will still drift on those invoices, even though INV-2291 now matches.

**Next step.** Finance should reconcile a Ledgerline export of multi-line invoices against both methods. If per-line is confirmed, sum `cents(line_net * rate)` per line in `invoice_totals`, and add a test for the two-0.05-lines case.

# NOTES: one-cent difference from Ledgerline (INV-2291)

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: the two `quantize` calls, in `line_net` and in the VAT line of `invoice_totals`, now pass `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP`. They previously used Decimal's default rounding, which is half-even.

## Why
- `docs/accounting-rules.md` (rule 2) says Ledgerline rounds half-up to the cent. With half-even, INV-2291's VAT of 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125 rounded to 0.12, giving a total of 1.37. With half-up it is 0.13 and the total is 1.38, which matches Ledgerline.
- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed. Before the change, `test_inv_2291` failed (1 failed, 2 passed).

## Not changed: VAT per line or on the subtotal
- Docs rule 4 says we don't know which method Ledgerline uses. VAT is still computed once on the subtotal.
- The findings mirror (entry 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412) says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, and reports a reconciliation of about 200 invoices. I could not verify that from this project. INV-2291 cannot tell the two methods apart, since both give 1.38 with half-up.
- The methods differ on, for example, two 0.05 lines at 10%: subtotal VAT gives a total of 0.11, per-line VAT gives 0.12. Finance can check one such invoice in Ledgerline. If per-line is confirmed, change the VAT line in `invoice_totals` to sum per-line VAT.

## Caveats
- Negative amounts round half away from zero (Decimal's ROUND_HALF_UP). The docs don't say how Ledgerline handles negatives; not checked.
- No test covers the line-level change. It was checked by hand: `line_net("0.5", "0.05")` gives 0.03.

`invoicing/totals.py` called `Decimal.quantize(CENT)` with no rounding argument, so it used the default decimal rounding, ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding). `docs/accounting-rules.md` says commercial rounding (half-up). `docs/accounting-rules.md` says we don't yet know whether Ledgerline computes VAT per line or once on the subtotal, and says not to change the method until finance confirms it. The code still computes VAT on the subtotal. The mirror note above says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, based on reconciling about 200 invoices. I did not adopt that: it is unconfirmed here and conflicts with our rule. INV-2291 gives 1.38 under both methods, so it cannot tell them apart. The methods do differ on some multi-line invoices: two 0.05 lines at 10% total 0.11 on the subtotal method and 0.12 per line.

## Open
- Only the rounding part is fixed. INV-2291 now matches Ledgerline. Other invoices with VAT may still differ until the method is confirmed.

## Other
- `ROUND_HALF_UP` rounds ties away from zero, so a negative tie (a credit note of -0.125) becomes -0.13. Ledgerline's handling of negative amounts is unverified.

# Notes: one-cent drift from Ledgerline

## What was wrong
Our totals differed from Ledgerline by one cent. For INV-2291 we had 1.37 and Ledgerline has 1.38. `invoicing/totals.py` called `Decimal.quantize(CENT)` with no rounding mode, so Python's default half-even rounding applied. INV-2291's VAT is 0.125 (1.25 × 0.10), which half-even rounds down to 0.12. `docs/accounting-rules.md` specifies half-up (commercial) rounding.

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: both `quantize` calls (in `line_net` and in the VAT calculation) now pass `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP`, with a comment explaining why.
- INV-2291 now gives VAT 0.13 and total 1.38. `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed.
- Side effect: `line_net` changes only for fractional quantities that land exactly on a half-cent. For example, 0.5 × 0.05 = 0.025 is now 0.03 (was 0.02). This follows the documented rule.

## Not changed: how VAT is computed
VAT is still computed once on the invoice subtotal. `docs/accounting-rules.md` says not to change this until finance confirms how Ledgerline does it. A findings-archive note (entry 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412) says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, and that half-up rounding alone still drifts on multi-line invoices. I did not apply that. I could not verify it: it reports a reconciliation against Ledgerline API v3, and we do not know our Ledgerline version.

## For finance
Please check one multi-line invoice against Ledgerline, for example two lines of 1 × 0.05 at 10% VAT. Our method gives a total of 0.11. Per-line VAT gives 0.12. If Ledgerline shows 0.12, the VAT method needs to change too.
